(1) src/haute/_databricks_io.py:33 `_TABLE_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^`?[\w-]+`?\.`?[\w-]+`?\.`?[\w-]+`?$")` — the `` `? `` tokens make each backtick optional, so BOTH `cat.schema.table` AND `` `cat`.`schema`.`table` `` (and partial-quoting mixes) pass. This same regex is the only gate at fetch_and_cache (line 297), routes/databricks.py:39 (_validate_table_param) and routes/files.py:194.

(2) _cache_path_for line 163: `safe_name = table.replace(".", "_").replace("/", "_").replace("\\", "_")` — backtick is NOT in the replace set. So `cat.schema.table` -> `cat_schema_table.parquet` while `` `cat`.`schema`.`table` `` -> `` `cat`_`schema`_`table`.parquet `` (two distinct files).

(3) Line 166 guard `if not safe_name or result.parent != cache_dir: raise ValueError(...)` does NOT fire: backtick is a legal filename character on Windows and POSIX, `safe_name` is non-empty, and `result.parent` is still the resolved cache_dir. No exception -> silent divergence.

(4) Both ends key off the raw `table` string through _cache_path_for: write side fetch_and_cache line 310 `out_path = _cache_path_for(table, ...)`; read side read_cached_table line 442 -> cached_path line 176 -> _cache_path_for. Runtime readers pass the config field verbatim: _io.py:414 `table = _required_config_string(config, "table", ...)` then _io.py:425 `read_cached_table(_table)`; also _builders.py:555. _required_config_string returns the stored string with NO normalization (grep found zero backtick-stripping anywhere in src/haute except the regex at line 33). So a fetch performed with the quoted form and a later read with the unquoted form (or vice versa) miss each other -> CacheNotFoundError or a redundant second fetch; two configs differing only by quoting maintain separate caches for identical data.

(5) Even the temp-file write tolerates it: tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f"{out_path.stem}.") (line 318) — backtick in the stem is a valid prefix, so the whole flow stays silent.

(6) Existing tests (tests/test_databricks_io.py:844-887, TestUnicodeTableNames) cover Unicode/homoglyph/zero-width-space collisions but never the backtick case (grep for backtick/`cat` in that file: no matches).
verdict.recommended_fix: In _cache_path_for, normalize away SQL backtick quoting before deriving safe_name so quoted and unquoted forms collapse to one cache key, e.g. `safe_name = table.replace("`", "").replace(".", "_").replace("/", "_").replace("\\", "_")`. Strip (remove) backticks rather than mapping them to "_" because backticks are pure SQL delimiters, not part of the identifier — `` `cat`.`schema`.`table` `` and `cat.schema.table` are the same logical table and must share one cache file. Add a regression test asserting `_cache_path_for("`cat`.`schema`.`table`") == _cache_path_for("cat.schema.table")` alongside the existing TestUnicodeTableNames cases. (Alternatively, but less ideal: normalize the table string once at the config boundary so the engine only ever sees one canonical form.)

verdict.evidence: Code-trace confirms the over-block. `_DANGEROUS_SQL_RE = re.compile(r"\b(DROP|DELETE|INSERT|UPDATE|...|LATERAL)\b", re.IGNORECASE)` (_databricks_io.py:36-39). `_validate_select_clause` (lines 72-84) runs `match = _DANGEROUS_SQL_RE.search(stripped)` (line 82) over the WHOLE query with zero string-literal/backtick awareness, raising `ValueError(f"Query contains forbidden SQL keyword: {match.group()!r}")` (line 84) on any hit. Regex `\b` is the boundary between a word char [A-Za-z0-9_] and a non-word char; `'` and backtick are both non-word chars. Trace for `"SELECT * FROM t WHERE status = 'DELETE'"`: startswith SELECT passes (73); no `;` (75); no `--` (78); no `/*` (80); then `\bDELETE\b` matches the DELETE inside `'DELETE'` (boundary at `'D` and `E'`) -> raises at 84. A legitimate read-only SELECT is rejected. Backtick variant ``SELECT `update` FROM t`` likewise fires `\bUPDATE\b`. Negative control holds: `update_ts` is NOT matched because trailing `_` is a word char (no boundary), so over-blocking is confined to the exact-keyword-as-data case. Reachability is closed: `FetchTableRequest.query` is unconstrained `str | None` (schemas.py:590) -> POST /api/databricks/fetch passes `body.query` (routes/databricks.py:160) -> `fetch_and_cache(query=...)` -> `_validate_select_clause(query)` (line 304). The `FROM {table}` is appended only after validation (line 308) and so does not change the matcher's view. No guard de-quotes literals before the denylist; the existing tests (test_databricks_io.py, test_security_gaps.py) only assert keywords-as-syntax are blocked and never cover keywords-as-literals, so nothing prevents the false positive.
verdict.recommended_fix: Strip SQL string literals (and optionally backtick-quoted identifiers) from the query before applying `_DANGEROUS_SQL_RE`, e.g. remove `'...'` / `"..."` spans (handling doubled-quote escapes) and `` `...` `` spans, then run the denylist on the remaining structural text. More principled long-term fix: replace the denylist with an allowlist column-list grammar parse, consistent with the module's documented "GUI config, not arbitrary SQL" constraint. Add tests asserting `SELECT * FROM t WHERE status = 'DELETE'` and ``SELECT `update` FROM t`` are accepted while `WHERE DELETE = 1` / bare `DELETE`/`UPDATE` keywords remain rejected.

verdict.evidence: Confirmed by code-trace. parse_column_path (src/haute/_api_input_schema.py:236-255) performs only three checks: (1) `if not column_path.startswith(table_path): raise` (236), (2) `tail = column_path[len(table_path):]; if not tail: raise` (242-248), (3) `if not tail.startswith("."): raise` (249-254), then `return tail.removeprefix(".")` (255). No check inspects the tail for an intermediate "[*]" array iterator. Trace of the cited example: parse_column_path('$[*].drivers[*].licenses[*].id', '$[*].drivers[*]') -> startswith True; tail = '.licenses[*].id' (non-empty, starts with '.'); returns 'licenses[*].id'. This violates the function's own docstring contract (lines 233-234): "Raises ApiInputSchemaError if the column's path doesn't sit cleanly under the table's iteration depth" — a column descending through the deeper `licenses[*]` array is NOT at the table's depth yet is accepted. Downstream, _json_shred._resolve_leaf(value, 'licenses[*].id') (src/haute/_json_shred.py:524-536): value is a dict; '.' in leaf -> loop over leaf.split('.') = ['licenses[*]', 'id']; first part cur = value.get('licenses[*]') -> None (real key is 'licenses', a list); second iteration cur is None -> `else: return None` (534-535). Result: the column resolves to None for every row, silently. Skeptical counter-checks found NO guard: parse_table_path (line 210) DOES enforce every segment ends with '[*]' but is never applied to the column tail; validate_v2_schema calls parse_column_path at line 366 as the ONLY column-path validity gate; grep confirms parse_column_path is the sole tail-validator (also used at _json_shred.py:574 and :819). The JSON cache route (routes/json_cache.py:15-20) explicitly accepts arbitrary user/editor-supplied v2 configs and converts ApiInputSchemaError into a structured 422 (B3, the on-the-wire contract) — but no error is raised here, so a malformed config slips through to produce silent-null columns at shred/cache-build time. infer_v2_schema_from_data never emits '[*]' in a column leaf (leaves come from scalar dict keys `cols[k]`; paths via _make_path at _json_shred.py:1188-1191), so this is reachable only via a hand-crafted/edited config — but that is exactly the input class the 422 contract is meant to police. Existing tests (tests/test_v2_codec_and_shred.py:66-82) cover only a clean leaf, a nested-dotted leaf, and an unrelated-prefix rejection; none exercises a tail containing '[*]'.
verdict.recommended_fix: In parse_column_path, after computing `tail` and stripping the leading dot, reject any leaf that still contains an array iterator: `leaf = tail.removeprefix("."); if "[*]" in leaf: raise ApiInputSchemaError("v2 column path crosses a nested array ('[*]' in leaf); the deeper array must be declared as its own table, columns must name a flat leaf under the table's iteration depth", column_path=column_path, table_path=table_path)`. This still permits legitimately dotted leaves like 'profile.age' (which contain no '[*]'), so the fix must key specifically on '[*]', not on the presence of dots. Add a failing test first (per project TDD guidance): assert parse_column_path('$[*].drivers[*].licenses[*].id', '$[*].drivers[*]') raises ApiInputSchemaError, plus a regression test that 'profile.age' still parses to 'profile.age'.

So "absent from the materialised frame" is one of several paths to the silent None, not the sole trigger; the validator-contract weakness itself is real.
verdict.recommended_fix: In validate_v2_schema, gate the row_id_column membership check on selected/emitting columns rather than all columns: maintain a parallel `selected_col_names` set (add cname only when `col.get("selected")`) and raise ApiInputSchemaError if row_id_column is not in it, with a message like "row_id_column=... must name a SELECTED column so it is emitted into the data port". This makes the validator loud-fail an unworkable config at cache-build time (structured 422) instead of yielding a silent null row identity in the trace UI.

verdict.evidence:
Code trace of src/haute/_edge_join.py:101-154 confirms both in-loop defensive branches are unreachable. Pre-loop guards establish the invariants:
- Line 107: `if len(source_ids) != len(target_handles): raise` → equal lengths (also makes `zip(..., strict=True)` at 132 safe).
- Line 114: `present_handles = [handle for handle in target_handles if handle is not None]` (order-preserving, drops only None).
- Line 117: `if len(present_handles) != len(target_handles): raise` → no None was dropped, so `present_handles == target_handles` element-for-element; therefore NO element of `target_handles` is None.
- Line 125: `if set(present_handles) != set(_ROLE_HANDLE_TO_CONFIG_KEY): raise`. `_ROLE_HANDLE_TO_CONFIG_KEY = {"base": "baseInput", "join": "joinInput"}` (lines 30-33), so `set(...) == {"base","join"}`. Combined with `present_handles == target_handles`, every element of `target_handles` ∈ {"base","join"}.

Loop branch 1 (lines 133-138 `if target_handle is None`): target_handle iterates target_handles, all non-None → UNREACHABLE.
Loop branch 2 (lines 140-145 `if config_key is None`): `_ROLE_HANDLE_TO_CONFIG_KEY.get(target_handle)` with target_handle ∈ {"base","join"} (exactly the dict keys) always returns "baseInput"/"joinInput" (non-None) → UNREACHABLE.
Only reachable in-loop raise is the genuine role/source mismatch at lines 147-154.

Call-graph: grep shows validate_edge_join_target_handles is defined at line 101 and invoked only at line 96 (resolve_edge_join_role_indices), which forwards target_handles unchanged — no other callers in src/.

Tests confirm: tests/test_edge_join.py:733 passes target_handles=["join","base"] (both non-None, both valid, swapped vs config) which clears all pre-loop guards and hits the line-147 raise (match="targetHandle.*baseInput"). The codegen test (lines 758-759) uses handles "join"/"base" the same way. A grep over the entire tests/ dir shows ["join","base"] is the ONLY target_handles value ever passed — no test supplies a None element or an invalid non-None handle, because those are rejected at lines 117/125 before the loop, exactly as claimed.
verdict.recommended_fix: Drop the two unreachable blocks (lines 133-138 and 140-145) and replace `config_key = _ROLE_HANDLE_TO_CONFIG_KEY.get(target_handle)` with a direct subscript `config_key = _ROLE_HANDLE_TO_CONFIG_KEY[target_handle]`, since membership in {"base","join"} is guaranteed by the line-125 check. The direct subscript additionally preserves fail-loud behavior (raises KeyError) if a future refactor breaks the upstream invariant, consistent with the repo's no-silent-fallback policy. The error messages removed are already emitted for the equivalent malformed inputs by the line-117 (None present) and line-125 (invalid/extra handle) raises, so behavior is preserved exactly. ~13 lines removed.

verdict.evidence: Traced the dual-failure path in src/haute/_worker_isolation.py:245-249: `cleanup_error = _run_cleanup_callbacks(...)`; `if primary_error is not None: if cleanup_error is not None: primary_error.add_note(str(cleanup_error)); raise primary_error`. The ONLY str() surfaced comes from IsolatedWorkerCleanupError.__init__ (lines 139-144): super().__init__(f"Isolated worker cleanup failed in {len(errors)} callback(s)", ...); self.errors = tuple(errors). Because IsolatedWorkerError.__init__ (line 55) does super().__init__(message), str(cleanup_error) is exactly the count message — no exception types, messages, or tracebacks. On this branch cleanup_error is NOT re-raised, NOT chained (no `raise ... from`), and its .errors tuple is dropped; the only `raise cleanup_error` is line 251 in the mutually-exclusive primary_error-is-None branch. Grep confirms .errors is consumed nowhere outside this module. Consumer trace makes the loss concrete: src/haute/routes/_background_jobs.py:198 catches the re-raised primary_error and records message=str(exc) (line 225) + fields from _isolated_worker_failure_fields (245-257), which reads worker_remote_traceback only for IsolatedWorkerRemoteError and never reads __notes__; since str(exc) does not include __notes__, even the count note is absent from the job record. No test exercises a raising cleanup callback alongside a primary error (tests/test_worker_isolation.py cleanups all succeed). Claim is proven; if anything the loss is marginally worse than described.
verdict.recommended_fix: On the dual-failure path, chain the cleanup error instead of dropping it: `raise primary_error from cleanup_error` so cleanup_error becomes __cause__ and its structured .errors tuple stays inspectable; optionally also enrich the note with per-error detail (e.g. join f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" over cleanup_error.errors). Extend _isolated_worker_failure_fields to record cleanup-error details when present. Add a regression test: primary failure + a raising cleanup callback must yield a raised error whose __cause__ (or note) exposes the underlying cleanup exception type/message.
